root_cause.text: The ICMP error handling code (icmp_socket_deliver in IPv4 and icmpv6_notify in IPv6) did not filter out packets whose inner protocol is IPPROTO_RAW (255), allowing a malicious ICMP message to be delivered to a raw socket opened with protocol IPPROTO_RAW, which was never intended to receive any data, leading to unintended FNHE cache modifications.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks `if (protocol == IPPROTO_RAW)` in icmp_socket_deliver and `if (nexthdr == IPPROTO_RAW)` in icmpv6_notify, causing such packets to be dropped with an ICMP error stat increment. The CVE description states that a raw socket using IPPROTO_RAW "MUST drop incoming ICMP" and that a malicious ICMP packet with inner protocol 255 can match the socket and lead to FNHE cache changes.
